title: At Nine, Manchester's Adrian Abraham Is Chasing a Grade 8 Guitar Record
excerpt: The Indian-origin Middleton schoolboy started playing two years ago. This month he sits the highest graded electric guitar exam — and a pass would make him the youngest ever to do it.
body:
• Adrian Abraham, a nine-year-old of Indian origin from Middleton, Greater Manchester, is preparing for the Trinity College London Grade 8 Rock & Pop electric guitar exam, the highest grade in the system.
  • A pass at nine would make him the youngest person ever to achieve Grade 8 on electric guitar — the current record holder, Alexander Hargraves of Colne, was 11 years and seven months old.
  • Adrian took up guitar about two years ago after watching his father, Abraham Joseph, play acoustic guitar; his favourite band is Iron Maiden and his showcase piece is Van Halen's Eruption.
  • He already holds artist sponsorships from Marshall Amplifiers and Solar Guitars, and posts performances of Metallica, Guns N' Roses, Queen and Deep Purple on Instagram.

Most nine-year-olds are still working through their first chord shapes. Adrian Abraham is preparing to walk into a Grade 8 electric guitar examination later this month, and if he passes, the Indian-origin schoolboy from Middleton, near Manchester, will enter the record books as the youngest person ever to reach the top grade on the instrument.

Two years from first chord to Grade 8

Adrian started playing only about two years ago, after watching his father, Abraham Joseph, play acoustic guitar at home. According to the Rochdale Times, his father recalled that the boy asked simply to hold the guitar to get the feel of it, held a clean chord at the first attempt, and moved from a classical acoustic to an electric guitar within about three months because the first instrument was no longer enough for him. Joseph, who sang in choirs and played acoustic guitar at college, taught him the basics; beyond that, Adrian largely taught himself as he climbed the grades.

"I just love playing the guitar and expressing myself through rock and metal music."

— Adrian Abraham

What Grade 8 actually demands

Grade 8 is the highest level in the graded music system and is normally taken by candidates several years older. Adrian is sitting the Trinity College London Grade 8 Rock & Pop electric guitar examination, which tests advanced technique, musical interpretation, sight-reading and aural skills. The record he is chasing was set earlier this year by Alexander Hargraves from Colne, England, who passed at 11 years and seven months — more than two years older than Adrian is now.

Rock first, but not rock only

Adrian's repertoire is unapologetically heavy: Iron Maiden are his favourite band, Van Halen's Eruption is his favourite piece to play, and his Instagram page carries performances of Metallica, Guns N' Roses, Queen, Deep Purple, Slipknot and System of a Down. He also sings and writes songs, and coverage of his playing notes that he mixes Western rock with Indian and Bollywood-inspired music. That range has brought industry backing well beyond a school music room: he holds official artist sponsorships from Marshall Amplifiers, the British amp maker behind decades of stadium rock, and from Solar Guitars, a brand favoured by metal players.

Why it resonates

For diaspora families, the shape of the story is familiar: a parent's revived hobby, a child who runs far past the parent's own level, and a front room that becomes a practice studio. Adrian has said his aim is to inspire other children to pick up an instrument. The exam comes first, though — a pass this month makes the Guinness World Record his; anything less, and a nine-year-old still has years in hand to try again.
